newsitem.title: USA: Abbott retrovirus test cleared by FDA.
newsitem.headline: Abbott retrovirus test cleared by FDA.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories Inc said Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) licensed for marketing the first blood screening test for detection of antibodies to both human T-lymphotropic virus types I and II (HTLV-1/HTLV-II).
HTLV-I is a retrovirus known to cause a rare form of leukemia and certain neurological disorders, Abbott said. HTLV-II is a retrovirus closely related to HTLV-I, it added.
Abbott said it already markets a test for HTLV-I alone.
Abbott said that recent studies have shown that HTLV-II has a suspected association with neurologic, hematologic, dermatologic and immunologic disorders.
HTLV-I and HTLV-II retroviruses are transmitted through sexual contact, shared needles among intravenous drug users, contaminated blood products and breast milk.
Abbott said its test can be run on Abbott instrument systems already in use for testing in most blood banks.
